headline: High: Goose can write and egress broadly while Great Expectations reads/writes shared data artifacts, creating default-path leakage and cascading misuse risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Goose can use MCP, read/write the filesystem, and runs with no default self-isolation; Great Expectations consumes files for validation results and documentation. A shared workspace makes malicious content in files or docs a plausible instruction bridge, though the interaction is indirect and not proven by evidence.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace directory
IF Goose ingests file or MCP content as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Disable MCP inputs for untrusted files
Add a provenance banner to all shared artifacts
Require manual review before Goose acts on file-derived instructions

B_data_leakage.rationale: Goose touches source code and files in cwd, handles model-provider and extension tokens, and has broad network egress; Great Expectations reads data sources and emits validation results. If they share files, sensitive data can flow from Goose-managed artifacts into Great Expectations outputs, but the profiles do not show automatic third-party upload by B.
conditions: IF Goose stores secrets or source code in the shared workspace
IF Great Expectations reads those files as validation inputs
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared directory
Mount separate read-only inputs for Great Expectations
Rotate any exposed model-provider or extension tokens
Restrict Goose network egress to approved endpoints

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can install packages, and Goose can write the filesystem and modify git state while Great Expectations can operate on files in the same workspace. That overlap creates default mutable-resource contention; no locking or coordination primitive is documented, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF both agents modify the same repository or dependency environment
IF no external lock serializes package installs or git writes
mitigations: Serialize package installs
Use separate virtual environments
Lock the git working tree during writes
Assign one agent read-only access to shared files

D_cascading_error.rationale: Goose can generate code or operational artifacts, and Great Expectations can consume files and produce validation results. If B treats A-produced outputs as authoritative, an error in Goose can cascade into incorrect validation or downstream decisions; the profiles do not show a verification gate by default.
conditions: IF Great Expectations consumes Goose-generated files as trusted inputs
IF no independent verification step checks those files before validation
mitigations: Insert a human review step before validation
Validate against a known-good schema
Compare outputs to a baseline snapshot
Mark Goose-generated artifacts as untrusted

E_compliance.rationale: Goose handles model-provider keys and extension tokens and has broad network egress, while Great Expectations is documented as touching data sources, validation results, and documentation. The pair can create compliance exposure if regulated data is placed into shared artifacts, but the profiles do not show a specific residency or certification mismatch.
conditions: IF regulated data is written into shared files
IF those files are processed by both agents under different retention or residency rules
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared workspaces
Apply a retention policy to validation outputs
Document data-class handling for both agents
Review network destinations for Goose
